list: Official 55-trophy list as published by PlayStation and mirrored by Exophase and PSNProfiles (checked 2026-11-18): 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze. There are no online trophies in this list.
sourcesNote: Every requirement below is taken from the official trophy description printed on the card. Strategy text is written for this guide. Source keys are expanded in the app: official = the official PS5 list via the Exophase mirror; psn = PSNProfiles trophy list and its tracked counts; wiki = GTA Wiki for Leonida place and term background; craft = the author's own strategy notes for this guide.

trophies.guide: The platinum is automatic: it unlocks the moment the other 54 trophies are all on your account, with nothing extra to do in the game itself. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap in this guide — clear the story, work the stranger strands, sweep the collectibles, then grind the activity and money totals, and this lands last. If it ever looks stuck, count your earned list against the 54 in this tracker rather than replaying anything.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
steps: Follow the seven roadmap stages in order
Use the tracker filters to find whatever is left
Earn trophy 54 and the platinum pops on its own

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission named in the official description, so this is simply a reward for starting the story and seeing the prologue through to its end. Play it slowly: the opener doubles as the game's tutorial for moving, driving and your partner, and nothing in it is timed or scored. It cannot be missed, because the campaign cannot begin any other way.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
steps: Start a new game and play the prologue
Follow the on-screen prompts through Gone Fishing
Trophy unlocks at the mission-complete screen

trophies.guide: A straight story-progress trophy for finishing Chapter 1, per the official description. While you are in this chapter, build the two habits that protect the whole run: keep a manual save at the start of each new mission, and try every side activity you pass once, which banks early progress toward Master of None and the 100% completion total. Chapter trophies are never missable — worst case, mission replay and chapter flow carry you back.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
steps: Play the story through the end of Chapter 1
Keep one manual save per mission start
Sample each new activity type as it appears

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2, exactly as the official description states (and yes, the asterisks are part of the published trophy name). By this chapter the map and your contact list are opening up, so start answering stranger markers between missions — the stranger strands finished later in the run are much shorter if you begin their early links now. Keep the rotating manual saves going, especially before any mission whose name matches a trophy in this list.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
steps: Complete every Chapter 2 story mission
Start stranger strands as their markers appear
Save manually before each new story mission

trophies.guide: Story progress again: see Chapter 3 through to its final mission. This is a good point in the run to pause the campaign for an hour and bank repeatable progress — a few Shooting Range challenges, your first races and some exploration of Leonida — because the activity trophies are pure totals and every early attempt counts. Nothing in the chapter itself can be permanently missed.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
steps: Finish the Chapter 3 mission chain
Bank early range, race and stunt attempts
Explore new districts as they open for The Goodtime State

trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4, per the official description. With the main arc nearing its end, check the missable-watch trophies in this guide before you push on: Catch Me If You Can belongs to a VCIA visit, and the choice-based Actions Speak Louder counter is fed by story decisions, so a mid-chapter save is cheap insurance. After this chapter only the endgame and the cleanup stages remain.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
steps: Play Chapter 4 to its conclusion
Keep a save before VCIA-related story beats
Log choices as you make them for Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: The gold story trophy: finish the final mission of the campaign, as the official description says. Before you start it, spend your cash and finish any strand you want resolved, because finales in this series can change the state of the world. Afterwards you return to free roam for the long cleanup, so nothing repeatable is lost by finishing — but your pre-finale save is the one to protect if a choice-based counter still worries you.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
steps: Reach and complete the final story mission
Save separately just before starting it
Return to free roam afterwards for cleanup stages

trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named story mission, and the official description asks only that you complete it — no medal, no time limit, no optional objective. If a section gives you trouble, lower your pace rather than restarting from a checkpoint repeatedly; mission trophies in this list reward finishing, not style. It sits early in the campaign flow, so most players earn it in the first sittings.
trophies.name: Trust
steps: Start Breakfast Run when it appears on the map
Play it through to the completion screen
No gold-medal or no-death condition applies

trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist, the set-piece heist mission named in the official description. Heists in this series usually offer approach choices; pick whichever crew and entry point you are comfortable with, because the trophy pays out for completion either way. A manual save before the planning stage lets you retry a different approach later without touching your main progress.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
steps: Unlock The Cartel Heist in the story
Choose any approach and finish the job
Trophy pops at mission complete, any approach counts

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Child's Play, as the official description requires. It is one of the named-mission trophies that simply tracks campaign progress, so it needs no preparation beyond arriving at it. If you are following the roadmap, it falls inside the Chapter 3 push, between Vice City, Baby! and the Chapter 4 trophies.
trophies.name: Family Matters
steps: Progress the story until Child's Play is offered
Complete the mission at any difficulty pace
Continue straight into the next story beat

trophies.guide: Complete Headliners, the named mission in the official description. Like the other single-mission story trophies it has no performance condition attached — finishing is the whole requirement. Because several named missions cluster in the middle chapters, use this stretch to keep your manual-save rotation tidy: one save before each named mission means a missed one-off moment is always a reload away, never a new playthrough.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
steps: Take on Headliners when the story offers it
Finish the mission to the results screen
Keep your per-mission save rotation going

trophies.guide: Finish VCIA Takedown, the airport-authority mission named in the official description — VCIA is the Vice City International Airport operation referenced by several trophies. Pay attention while you are on VCIA ground: the separate Catch Me If You Can trophy asks for an unscheduled departure from the same place, and a story visit is the most natural chance to arrange it. Save before this mission so you can experiment inside it.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
steps: Save before starting VCIA Takedown
Complete the mission as directed
Watch for the unscheduled-departure opening for Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory, per the official description — another named-mission progress trophy with no extra condition. It is the last of the individually named story missions in the official list, so once it pops your remaining story work is the chapter finishes and the finale. That makes it a natural checkpoint to review the tracker: everything left should be strands, collectibles, activities and grinds.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
steps: Play Operation Savage Glory to completion
Review the tracker for leftover story items
Move on to the stranger-strand stage of the roadmap

trophies.guide: The second gold, and the real spine of the platinum: reach 100% completion as the official description demands. In this series the completion counter is a checklist of story, strands, hobbies, collectibles and miscellaneous tasks — almost everything else in this trophy list feeds it. Work it last-but-continuously: keep the in-game completion screen open beside this tracker, clear categories in bulk, and hunt the final missing percent by category rather than by wandering.
trophies.name: A Long Road
steps: Finish story and all stranger strands first
Clear collectibles and activities category by category
Compare the in-game 100% screen with this tracker to find the gap

trophies.guide: A pure volume trophy: complete 250 stunts, as the official description counts them. Stunts are the game's jump and stunt opportunities scattered across Leonida, and they are repeatable, so this is a routing problem, not a skill wall. Learn a dense loop of ramps in one district, run it whenever you pass through, and save the scattered rural stunts for the exploration sweep — the counter only cares about the total.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
steps: Learn one dense urban stunt loop early
Run stunts opportunistically while travelling
Sweep leftover districts during the collectibles stage

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every activity type once — the official description says each type, and the published list summary counts nine activity types. You do not need to win or finish most of them; starting each distinct activity registers it. Keep a note in this tracker of which types you have touched, because the game does not show a tidy per-type checklist, and the last forgotten type is always the one nobody remembers trying.
trophies.name: Master of None
steps: Start each new activity the first time you pass one
Note the type in the tracker as you try it
Chase the final untried type with the activity filter on

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The hardest skill trophy on the list: gold medals in every Shooting Range challenge — 42 of them, per the count the official listing tracks. Treat each weapon category separately, learn a range's target pattern with a few silver runs, then push for gold once the rhythm is set. Accuracy bonuses usually matter more than raw speed, so slow down until a category is consistent, then speed up. Progress is permanent per challenge, so chip away at it across the whole playthrough.
trophies.name: The Shootist
steps: Clear each range challenge to silver while learning patterns
Return category by category for gold pushes
Prioritise accuracy bonuses over speed until consistent
trophies.target: gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location — 14 locations in the published count. Unlike the general race trophy, this one is per-location, so a win only counts once per course and re-winning a favourite course does nothing. Fly each course once slowly to learn its gates before racing it properly, and mark locations off in the tracker, because fourteen similar courses blur together fast.
trophies.name: Top Fun
steps: Scout each drone course once at low speed
Race for the win once the gate line is familiar
Tick off each of the 14 locations in the tracker
trophies.target: a win at all 14 Top Fun drone race locations

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — the word different in the official description is the whole catch: repeating one easy race twenty times does not count. Spread your wins across race types and districts, use a vehicle you have upgraded for each class, and let these wins double as map exploration for The Goodtime State. If a race keeps beating you, come back with a better vehicle rather than grinding it frustrated.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
steps: Win each race once instead of repeating favourites
Match an upgraded vehicle to each race class
Track the 20 distinct wins as you go

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge, as the official description puts it — a head-to-head against a named character rather than a score target. Fishing challenges are repeatable, so learn the casting and reeling timing on a first attempt with no pressure, then challenge Cal again when the mechanic feels natural. Upgrade your tackle if the game offers it; small gear differences decide close catches.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
steps: Practise fishing until the reeling timing clicks
Start Cal's fishing challenge
Retry freely — the challenge can be re-attempted
trophies.target: a fishing challenge win against Cal

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — the simplest activity trophy on the list. The official description asks for a completion, not a high score, so pick the shortest cabinet you find, learn its one mechanic, and finish a full run. Arcades sit inside other locations you will visit for shopping and story beats, so this usually pops during ordinary exploration once you stop walking past the machines.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
steps: Find an arcade cabinet during exploration
Play one game through to its end screen
Any cabinet and any score counts

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's mission strand — the official description requires his final mission, which means the whole chain before it, not a single job. Stranger and contact strands unlock in links, often after a wait or a phone call, so if Andy goes quiet, advance time and keep playing rather than assuming the strand is broken. Completing strands like this also feeds Strangers & Freaks and the 100% counter.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
steps: Start Andy's strand when his marker appears
Work each link as it unlocks
Complete his final mission to pop the trophy

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission, per the official description — again a full strand, not one job. The boat-flavoured trophy name hints his work stays near the water, so expect his links around marinas and the coast. As with every strand, do the links as they appear instead of saving them all for the endgame; strands are gated by story progress and in-game time, and starting early means they are ready when you want them.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
steps: Pick up Kenton's strand at his first marker
Follow the chain through its waiting periods
Finish his final mission

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's strand by completing his final mission, exactly as the official description states. Billy is one of the five named contacts with a personal trophy, and his chain counts toward both Strangers & Freaks and 100% completion, so it is never wasted time. If you are batching strands, alternate Billy's links with another contact's — the downtime between links overlaps neatly.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
steps: Begin Billy's missions when introduced
Complete each link as it becomes available
Play his final mission through to the end

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight full stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida — the silver counts strands, not individual missions, per the official description. The five named-contact trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are strands too, so finishing those plus any three other strangers lands this. Start strands early: most are chains with waiting time between links, and a strand you never started is the only kind that can stall your endgame.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
steps: Start every stranger marker you pass
Finish the five named contacts' strands first
Add any three more strands to reach eight

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission, as the official description requires — the whole of his strand. Randy's name and the supply-and-demand title suggest delivery and goods work, the kind of chain that sends you across the map; combine his trips with exploration and vehicle discovery so the driving does double duty for The Goodtime State and Whip It Good. Finish the strand before the finale for a tidier endgame.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
steps: Start Randy's strand on first contact
Complete links as they unlock
Finish his final mission

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's strand through his final mission, per the official description. Tyrone is the fifth named contact with a dedicated trophy; together the five strands are the backbone of the Strangers & Freaks silver and a solid slice of 100% completion. Keep one strand active at all times — an idle map with no strand link available usually means a link is waiting on a phone call or a sleep cycle.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
steps: Open Tyrone's strand when he appears
Work the chain to its final mission
Complete the finale of the strand

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot in Leonida — 18 spots in the published count. These are fixed locations, so treat them like a collectible set: sweep them district by district during the exploration stage and mark each one in the tracker, because the game gives no per-spot checklist you can trust at a glance. Spots sit in scenic places, so a meditation sweep doubles as area discovery for The Goodtime State.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
steps: Sweep meditation spots district by district
Meditate fully at each spot until it registers
Record each of the 18 in the tracker

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret sends you after, per the official description. Unique-animal hunts in this series are scripted encounters rather than random spawns: follow Bret's strand until the hunt itself begins, track the animal by the clues the mission gives you, and bring a weapon suited to a clean kill. If the trail goes cold, leave and re-enter the area to reset the encounter rather than circling the same ground.
trophies.name: Fair Game
steps: Advance Bret's hunting strand to the unique hunt
Follow the mission's tracking clues
Take the unique animal down to complete it
trophies.target: the unique animal hunt for Bret

trophies.guide: Complete three full collectible card sets — the silver asks for sets, not loose cards, so a pile of singles from ten sets is worth nothing until sets close. Pick the three smallest or most clustered sets first, sweep them in one route each, and log cards in the tracker by set so you can see which set is two cards from done. Cards are permanent pickups: none are missable, they are only easy to lose track of.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
steps: Choose the three most clustered card sets
Sweep one set per route, logging each card
Close all three sets to pop the trophy

trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 different locations, per the official description and its tracked count of 100. Like the race trophy, the locations are the point — repeating it in one spot does not move the counter. Build the habit of doing it once in every new place you visit: shops, strand locations, viewpoints, race starts. One per new location, logged in the tracker, turns a silver grind into background progress.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
steps: WAiNK It once in every new location you enter
Never farm repeats in a single spot
Check the tracker total weekly against the in-game count

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges, as the official description counts them. Challenges are the game's short-form objectives layered over free roam, and they accumulate naturally if you accept them as they appear instead of dismissing the prompts. When you need to force progress, open the challenges list and pick the nearly-done ones — the last ten completions are always faster from half-finished challenges than from fresh ones.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
steps: Accept challenge prompts as they appear in free roam
Review the challenge list for nearly-complete entries
Push the total to 50 with the shortest remaining challenges

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a four-star wanted level while your partner is with you, and fully escape — the official description needs both the partner and the escape. Deliberately set it up: commit crimes together until four stars, then break line of sight, swap vehicles away from witnesses and wait out the search in a quiet area. Doing it by accident usually fails on the partner condition, so stage it on your own terms in a part of the map you know well.
trophies.name: Hot Together
steps: Travel with your partner as a duo
Raise a wanted level to exactly four stars or more
Break sight, change vehicle and wait out the search
trophies.target: lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner present

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a row with your partner, without your wanted level dropping in between — the official description makes continuity the challenge. Plan a tight triangle of shops in one neighbourhood, rob the first, drive straight to the second while still wanted, then the third, and only escape after the third register is empty. Losing the stars between shops resets the chain, so speed matters more than the take.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
steps: Pick three shops close together in one district
Rob them in one unbroken wanted streak with your partner
Escape only after the third robbery registers
trophies.target: 3 shops robbed back-to-back, wanted level kept

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — a discovery counter, so each model counts once, per the official description's total. Enter or drive every new model you see parked or passing, favour rich districts and the airport for variety, and use story and strand missions, which hand you unusual vehicles for free. The tracker cannot name the models for you, but the in-game stat does count them; check it after each new district.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
steps: Get into every unfamiliar vehicle model you pass
Hunt variety in rich districts, marinas and VCIA
Use mission vehicles — they count as discoveries too

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Drop five enemies during one Combat Focus activation, as the official description requires. The trick is staging: find a spot where at least five enemies are grouped before you trigger it — a gang operation or a busy mission firefight — line up your first targets, then activate and work left to right without repositioning. If a run ends at four, reload the same encounter; the setup, not your aim, is usually the problem.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
steps: Find an encounter with five or more grouped enemies
Pre-aim the first targets before activating Combat Focus
Chain all five takedowns before the effect ends
trophies.target: 5 takedowns in one Combat Focus use

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE WATCH — built from the wording of the official description: an unscheduled departure at VCIA sounds like a one-off story moment, not a free-roam routine, so treat your story visits to the airport as the chance. VCIA is the airport tied to the VCIA Takedown mission; when a mission puts you on its ground with a plane or vehicle nearby, taking off outside the script is the natural reading of this trophy. Keep a manual save before every VCIA story beat, and if a departure opportunity appears, take it before completing the objective. If you finish the story without it, that pre-mission save is your way back.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
steps: Save before every VCIA story mission, including VCIA Takedown
On VCIA ground, watch for a chance to depart outside the script
Take the unscheduled departure before finishing the objective

trophies.guide: The official description is a joke at face value — it gets hot in these Rhinos, Rhino being the series' name for its battle tank — so the honest guide is: this is a hidden-style one-off tied to tanks, and the reliable way to earn it is to seek out a Rhino encounter in free roam or a high-heat escape and interact with the tank on its own terms. Raise your wanted level to military response if that is what brings armour out, or revisit any mission that fields one. Because the description is deliberately vague, keep it for the cleanup stage and try tank encounters both as driver and on foot.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
steps: Find a Rhino during a high-heat response or armoured mission
Engage with the tank encounter instead of fleeing it
Retry in free roam — tank spawns are repeatable

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — the official description makes stealth the entire condition. Scout the store first: note staff, cameras and the till, enter quietly, keep the robbery fast and leave before an alarm state counts as detection. If a run is blown, walk away and try another store rather than fighting it out; jewelry stores are repeatable targets and a clean quiet run is shorter than a loud one plus an escape.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
steps: Scout a jewelry store's staff and camera layout
Rob it quietly and quickly, avoiding detection
Leave clean — repeat at another store if detected

trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape after each, per the official description — a robbery only counts when you get away, so plan the exit before the entrance. Learn one vault's layout cold, then rotate banks so police response patterns stay predictable, and stage a fast, anonymous vehicle a street away for every job. Five clean getaways, logged one by one in the tracker, earn the silver.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
steps: Plan an exit vehicle before entering each bank
Rob the vault and escape to clear the wanted level
Repeat at five vaults, logging each success

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape, as the official description says. Armored trucks are free-roam events: when one appears, block it, deal with the guards, breach the rear doors, take the cash and leave the area fast — the escape is part of the requirement, so do not linger looting. Bring a vehicle with some durability and a weapon that opens the truck quickly; the whole event is over in a couple of minutes when prepared.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
steps: Watch for an armored truck in free roam
Stop it, clear the guards and breach the doors
Take the cash and escape the area
trophies.target: one armored truck robbery with escape

trophies.guide: Explore the whole state — 52 areas in the published count behind the official description 'Explore all of Leonida'. Areas register by entering them, so this is a coverage sweep: work the map in a grid during the collectibles stage, and let strand missions, races and card routes do most of it for you. The last areas are always the small rural ones nobody drives through on purpose, so finish with a deliberate border-to-border road trip.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
steps: Let missions and collectible routes uncover most areas
Sweep the map in a grid for untouched districts
Finish with a rural road trip for the final areas

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation from each gang — nine gangs in the published count. Variety is the requirement: robbing the same gang nine times does nothing, so log which gangs you have hit in the tracker and deliberately travel for the missing ones. Operations are defended, so arrive with full health, armour and a getaway plan, and expect the last two gangs to be the ones whose territory you rarely visit.
trophies.name: Pest Control
steps: Rob one operation and note its gang in the tracker
Target operations in territories you have not hit
Complete all nine gangs, one operation each
trophies.target: one illegal operation robbed per gang (9 gangs)

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — the official description names the place and the act, and trophies worded like this in the series are quiet one-off interactions rather than challenges. Head to Ocean Beach, find the bar or spot that offers a drink with the ocean view, and take it. If nothing prompts, try the beachfront venues at a relaxed hour and interact with what is offered; it costs a drink's price and a minute of standing still.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
steps: Travel to Ocean Beach on the coast
Find the beachfront drink spot with the view
Order and enjoy the cocktail until it registers
trophies.target: a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE WATCH — the official description describes a single cinematic act: smashing out of a vehicle showroom in a vehicle, in classic style. If a story mission ever places you inside a showroom with a car, that is very likely the scripted chance, so keep a save before showroom story beats and drive out through the window rather than the door. In free roam, test any enterable showroom the same way — get in a display car and exit through the glass. Treat it as missable until you have proven a free-roam showroom works.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
steps: Save before any story beat set in a vehicle showroom
Take a car inside the showroom
Drive out through the showroom glass, not the door
trophies.target: a vehicle showroom escape, through the glass

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Visit the Kolt & Associates bowling alley named in the official description and complete the follow-through it asks for — in plain terms, go bowling there properly rather than just entering the building. Play a game at that specific alley; other alleys, if any exist, are not the one the trophy names. It is a short detour on the cleanup route and pairs naturally with the arcade and meditation stops nearby.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
steps: Travel to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley
Start a bowling game at that alley
Play it through so the follow-through registers
trophies.target: a follow-through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley

trophies.guide: MISSABLE WATCH — the official description is deliberately cryptic: a partnership moment with mass appeal. Read plainly, it points at something you and your partner do together in front of an audience or crowd, which is exactly the kind of scripted story beat that may not repeat in free roam. Protect yourself the cheap way: keep a manual save before major partner missions, and whenever a mission puts the duo in front of a crowd, a camera or a stage, take the performative option. If it pops in free roam instead, the save cost you nothing.
trophies.name: Personal Best
steps: Save before major partner story missions
In crowd or camera moments, choose the showy partnership option
Check the trophy after each big duo set piece
trophies.target: a partnership moment with mass appeal

trophies.guide: MISSABLE WATCH — this tracks choices made, and PlayStation's counter for it runs to 500, far more than a single story playthrough of decisions is likely to hold. The risk the flag warns about is real but manageable: if choices only come from story and strand decisions, a careless single run could end short with nothing left to choose. Hedge from the start — make every optional choice the game offers, in dialogue, missions and free-roam encounters, never skipping an optional decision, and keep a pre-finale save so a second partial run stays possible if the counter stalls.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
steps: Take every optional choice offered from the opening onwards
Never skip dialogue or decision prompts
Keep a pre-finale save in case the 500 total needs a second run
trophies.target: choices made (PlayStation tracks a count to 500)

trophies.guide: MISSABLE WATCH — 'second time's the charm' reads as: fail at something specific, then succeed at it on the retry. Trophies phrased this way usually attach to one scripted attempt — a race, a job, a challenge with a story flavour — and the danger is succeeding first time and never getting the scripted fail. You cannot plan the exact spot from the description alone, so play naturally, and when any scripted attempt fails, retry it immediately and cleanly rather than moving on; if a named event allows a deliberate first failure, that is the safest place to earn it.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
steps: When a scripted attempt fails, retry it straight away
Win the retry rather than abandoning the event
If it never triggers, revisit repeatable named events in cleanup

trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the official description is a wink, and trophies like this in the series are earned by being present at one of the game's scripted oddities: a weird encounter out in the wilds rather than anything in a menu. Spend time in remote Leonida at night during the exploration stage, investigate any unusual marker, light or sound instead of driving past, and stay until the event finishes. It is a cleanup-stage trophy by nature: unhurried exploration is the whole method.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
steps: Explore remote areas at night during the map sweep
Investigate strange lights, sounds and markers
Stay and watch the event through to its end

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by — hitting a pedestrian target with a melee attack from a moving vehicle, per the official description's bowling joke. Ride or drive slowly past a target, swing the melee attack as you pass, and make sure the hit itself connects from the vehicle rather than after dismounting. It takes a few passes to learn the timing; use a quiet street and a willing volunteer of an NPC, and it is done in minutes.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
steps: Take a vehicle that allows melee attacks from it
Pass a pedestrian at low speed
Land the melee hit during the drive-by
trophies.target: a melee drive-by knockdown from a vehicle

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder a quarter of a million dollars of Marked Bills through your contacts — the official description names both the amount and the method, so ordinary spending money does not count; only bills pushed through the laundering route do. Unlock the contact route as early as the game allows, feed every batch of marked bills through it as they arrive from robberies, and never sit on a stockpile. Robbery trophies and this one feed each other, so run them in the same stage.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
steps: Unlock the laundering route through your contacts
Send every batch of Marked Bills through it promptly
Track the laundered total until it passes $250,000

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across the game's shops, per the official description. This is a money-sink trophy, so do not hoard: buy vehicles, upgrades, clothing and supplies as you play instead of saving for an endgame splurge, and the total arrives on its own. If you reach the cleanup stage short, vehicle and property-adjacent purchases burn the remainder fastest. Every dollar in any shop counts, so there is no wrong way to spend it.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
steps: Buy upgrades and vehicles as you go, not at the end
Spread spending across different shop types
Top up with big purchases if cleanup finds you short

trophies.guide: Buy every garage property — eight in the published count. Garages unlock for purchase as the map opens, so note each one as it appears and buy on sight once your robbery income is flowing; the expensive ones are why the money stage of the roadmap comes before this finishes. Owning them all also gives you storage for the vehicle collection that Whip It Good has you discovering, so the two trophies support each other.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
steps: Note each garage as it becomes available
Buy garages as robbery income allows
Own all eight to pop the trophy

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app, as the official description says. Registration is a per-vehicle action, so make it a habit: every time you acquire a vehicle you intend to keep, register it on the spot — the trophy's name is the method. Ten keepers accumulate quickly once garages from Little Boxes give you somewhere to put them, and registering early beats hunting for ten vehicles at the end.
trophies.name: On the Spot
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app when you acquire a vehicle
Register each keeper vehicle immediately
Reach ten registered vehicles
trophies.target: 10 vehicles registered on the Scooter Bros app
